pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Introduce the goe framework, summarise its architecture, list its major capabilities, and explain how the key subsystems relate to each other

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Guide a new user from zero to a running goe application, covering prerequisites and the minimal setup path

pages.title: Installation
pages.purpose: Explain the go get command, Go version requirement, module path, and any build-time prerequisites

pages.title: Quick Start Tutorial
pages.purpose: Walk through a minimal working application using goe.New and goe.Run with HTTP, configuration, and logging enabled

pages.title: Project Structure
pages.purpose: Describe the conventional layout of a goe project, the purpose of the core/, contract/, webresult/, and modules/ directories, and where user code lives

pages.title: Core Concepts
pages.purpose: Explain the foundational design principles of goe: dependency injection, the module contract, configuration loading, and the global accessor pattern

pages.title: Application Bootstrap
pages.purpose: Detail the goe.New(Options) constructor, every field of the Options struct, the goe.Run() call, global accessor functions, and how the singleton instance is managed

pages.title: Dependency Injection with Fx
pages.purpose: Explain how go.uber.org/fx powers the DI container, how Providers and Invokers are declared and resolved, and how the framework-provided contract interfaces are injected

pages.title: Module System and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Describe the contract.Module interface (Name, OnStart, OnStop, ValidateConfig, Provide), how built-in modules are registered, and the startup and shutdown ordering guarantee

pages.title: Configuration Hierarchy
pages.purpose: Explain how config is loaded from .env, .local.env, .{GOE_ENV}.env and system environment variables, the priority order, typed accessors (GetString, GetInt, GetBool, GetDuration), hot-reload, and the ConfigSource extension point

pages.title: Logging with Zap
pages.purpose: Cover the contract.Logger interface, the zap-backed implementation, log levels, JSON vs console format, file and stdout outputs, structured fields (With, WithContext, WithError), and the log.Module Fx integration

pages.title: HTTP Server
pages.purpose: Overview of the HTTP subsystem built on Fiber, listing the capabilities covered in sub-pages

pages.title: HTTP Kernel Overview
pages.purpose: Describe the contract.HTTPKernel interface, the HTTPConfig struct fields, server startup/shutdown lifecycle, default middleware registration, and RegisterDefaultConstraints

pages.title: Routing and Handlers
pages.purpose: Explain how to register routes on fiber.App, use the Group wrapper, the RouteRegistrar DI pattern, RegisterRoutes helper, and the HandlerParams injection struct

pages.title: Dependency Injection in Handlers
pages.purpose: Document the Services struct, InjectServices middleware, GetServices/GetConfig/GetLogger/GetCache/GetApp helpers, the AsHandler generic, and the Group DI routing methods

pages.title: Middleware System
pages.purpose: Cover the default request-logger and recover middleware, how to add custom middleware, SetupServiceMiddleware, and the available optional middleware (OIDC, CacheControl)

pages.title: Request Validation
pages.purpose: Explain the HTTPValidator interface, struct validation via go-playground/validator, built-in route constraints (uuid, uint, slug, email), and how validators are injected into handlers

pages.title: Response Utilities
pages.purpose: Document the webresult package in full: the WebResult struct, Map and List type aliases, SendSucceed, SendFailed, and the fiber.Error generators (InvalidParam, Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound, SystemBusy)

pages.title: Error Handling
pages.purpose: Cover the default Fiber error handler, the embedded error page HTML template and its data fields (Title, Code, Message, HomeLink), and how to customise error responses

pages.title: SPA and Static File Serving
pages.purpose: Document the spa middleware (Root, Index, NotFoundFile, MaxAge, Browse, Compress, ByteRange), the CacheControl middleware and CacheRule patterns, and how to serve a frontend app alongside an API

pages.title: Data Persistence
pages.purpose: Overview of the SQL, MongoDB, and migration modules, and how they fit into the application lifecycle

pages.title: SQL Database with GORM
pages.purpose: Cover DatabaseModule setup, supported drivers (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server), multi-connection configuration, DSN construction, connection pooling, auto-migration, RegisterModelsForMigration, and the contract.DB interface

pages.title: MongoDB Integration
pages.purpose: Describe the MongoDB DatabaseModule, default and named connections, pool settings (MIN_POOL_SIZE, MAX_POOL_SIZE, MAX_CONN_IDLE_TIME), debug command monitoring, the contract.MongoDB interface, and the utility functions for indexes, transactions, and bulk writes

pages.title: MongoDB Migrations
pages.purpose: Document the Migrator, Migration definition (New, Up, Down, Register), the contract.Migrator interface methods (Up, Down, Reset, Redo, Status, DryRun, VerifyChecksums), distributed locking via MongoLock, checksum verification, and the full set of migration helper functions

pages.title: Caching
pages.purpose: Overview of the caching subsystem, its driver model, and contract interfaces

pages.title: Cache Module and Drivers
pages.purpose: Explain the CacheManager, supported built-in drivers (memory, Redis, Memcache, database backends), the Extend method for custom drivers, and all relevant configuration keys (CACHE_STORE, CACHE_DRIVER, CACHE_PREFIX, CACHE_TTL, per-store settings)

pages.title: Cache Operations
pages.purpose: Document every method on contract.Cache: Get, GetWithDefault, Set, Forever, Forget, Flush, Has, Remember, RememberForever, Pull, Add, Increment, Decrement, and the typed cache wrapper

pages.title: Background Jobs
pages.purpose: Overview of the Redis-backed background job processing system and how it differs from the event system

page_notes.content: Eventing system has been removed since 2.0.2 release. Job system took over what we implemented in the eventing system.

pages.title: Job System Architecture
pages.purpose: Describe the Manager, Redis storage model, job state machine (pending→running→completed/failed/cancelled), the worker pool, the Promoter goroutine, the DLQ, and all configuration parameters

pages.title: Dispatching Jobs
pages.purpose: Cover JobDefinition, the JobBuilder fluent API (NewJob, OnQueue, WithDelay, WithSchedule, Unique, MaxAttempts, Timeout), Dispatch, DispatchMany, Cancel, and uniqueness deduplication
